html:
Amílcar Cabral was an agronomist and political thinker who led the fight for the independence of Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde from Portugal. He was murdered in 1973, months before Guinea-Bissau declared independence.

Born in Portuguese Guinea to Cape Verdean parents, he studied agriculture in Lisbon, where he met other students from the Portuguese colonies who went on to lead movements in Angola and Mozambique. As a colonial agronomist he surveyed the farms of Guinea, and learned the country village by village.

In 1956 he co-founded the PAIGC. When peaceful protest was met with massacre, it took up arms in 1963 and in time controlled much of the countryside, setting up schools, clinics and people's stores there. This colonial war in Africa drained Portugal.

Cabral wrote on culture as resistance and on the "return to the source". He was killed in Conakry in January 1973 by members of his own party, with Portuguese involvement suspected. After the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon in 1974, Portugal recognised Guinea-Bissau, and Cape Verde became independent in 1975.
sum: Amílcar Cabral was an agronomist and political thinker who led the fight for the independence of Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde from Portugal. He was murdered in 1973, months before Guinea-Bissau declared independence.
